name: King of Shimron-meron
overview: The King of Shimron-meron was a male ruler noted in the book of Joshua as one of thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. While his tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded, his defeat signifies the fulfillment of God's promise to give the Israelites the land. There are no additional notes providing further background on his life or reign.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Shimron-meron' directly identifies him as the ruler of the city or region called Shimron-meron. This name is a straightforward designation without a special meaning given beyond its literal sense, as recorded in Joshua 12:20.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Shimron-meron beyond what is listed in his unique attribute as a defeated king. No relatives or tribal connections are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: This king's significance lies in his inclusion among the thirty-one kings conquered by Joshua, marking the successful fulfillment of God's command to Israel to take possession of the Promised Land. His defeat underscores the divine authority working through Joshua as God's appointed leader. The mention of his kingship in Joshua 12:20 serves to document the extent of Israel's conquest and God's faithfulness in delivering their enemies into their hands.
